prerequisites: It is recommended not to take this course until having achieved the most complete possible vision of the technical disciplines taught in the degree.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to draft, sign and develop projects in the field of industrial engineering for the construction, reform, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly or operation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, industrial installations and plants, and manufacturing processes.
Ability to direct the activities that are the object of the engineering projects described in the previous section.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, and critical reasoning.
Ability to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Engineering, both orally and in writing, and to all types of audiences.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Ability to apply quality principles and methods.
Ability to organize and plan within the company, and other institutions and organizations.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding, and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.
Ability for the prevention of occupational hazards and protection of the health and safety of workers and users.
Honesty, responsibility, ethical commitment, and solidarity spirit.
Ability to work in a team.
Knowledge and skills to organize and manage projects. Know the organizational structure and functions of a project office.
Understand the requirements and legal and ethical implications of professional engineering practice, particularly in project development.
Know the characteristics of projects, their life cycle, and the technical, economic, safety, environmental, legal, social, and ethical conditions to be considered in them.

Define the scope of a project and plan the deadlines and costs of all necessary tasks to carry it out, and carry out progress control and supervision of the work to be done in a project, keeping the initial planning in mind.
Clearly explain and adequately justify the solutions adopted in a project, preparing the associated documents that allow its contracting and execution.
Know the structure and functions of a technical office, as well as develop and improve a work method.

syllabus_topics: Topic 4 Project Life Cycle. Preliminary Studies
Topic 5 Project Life Cycle. Engineering and Execution
Topic 7: Regulatory Framework and Project Processing.
teaching_methods: Classroom practices for problem-solving and case studies
Computer lab practices for planning, budgeting, graphic tools, and document management

assessment_methods.method: Non-contact work (EV-2). Practical skills (two individual assignments)
Laboratory Practices (EV-3). Practical skills (exercises and exam)

assessment_rules: To pass, a minimum of 5 out of 10 points must be obtained in each of the three parts (EV-1, EV-2, EV-3). If these minimums are met, the final grade is calculated as: Note = 0.4 x EV-1 + 0.35 x EV-2 + 0.25 x EV-3. Otherwise, the final grade will be the minimum between the calculated note and 4.0. For EV-2, the average of the two individual assignments is taken, provided each assignment scored above 4.0; otherwise, the score is the minimum of the average and 4.0. For EV-3, the grade is 0.5 x (exercises performed in class) + 0.5 x (Laboratory Practices exam). In the extraordinary examination, if a grade greater than 5 is obtained in any of the evaluable elements (EV-1, EV-2, EV-3) in the ordinary examination, this grade can be kept. For students with differentiated evaluation, mandatory attendance to practices is waived; their EV-3 is 0.25 x (exercises submitted) + 0.75 x (Laboratory Practices exam) in the ordinary call, and the exam score only in the extraordinary call.
